official_sources: Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Areas Act 1979
Historic England scheduled monuments owners guidance

official_measurement_examples.name: Current national collection
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Data reported 20,150 scheduled monuments with collector and new-data activity on 24 July 2026.

official_measurement_examples.name: SMC separate from planning
official_measurement_examples.fact: Historic England states most works to a scheduled monument require Scheduled Monument Consent from the Secretary of State, while some change may separately require planning permission from the local planning authority.

official_measurement_examples.name: Current GIS version
official_measurement_examples.fact: Historic England's public GIS downloads list scheduled-monument data as updated 14 July 2026; older cached geometry must retain its version date.

official_measurement_examples.name: Class Consent scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Some continuing agricultural or gardening operations may be covered by Class Consent, but this does not create a general exemption for other works.

official_measurement_examples.name: Section 42 distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Metal detecting and certain geophysical survey activity on scheduled monuments can require separate Section 42 consent, including where SMC exists.

official_measurement_examples.name: Designation versus ownership
official_measurement_examples.fact: Scheduling protects archaeological significance and does not identify freehold ownership, public access rights or development capacity.

official_measurement_examples.name: Geometry limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: National GIS is authoritative designation evidence but does not replace proposal-specific archaeological assessment, survey or checking the current NHLE entry.

official_measurement_examples.name: Consent conditions and expiry
official_measurement_examples.fact: SMC may carry conditions and can cease to have effect if works are not begun within the specified period; a historic consent must not be assumed current without checking its terms.

core_rules: scheduled designation is not land ownership evidence
SMC is distinct from planning permission
Class Consent is activity-specific not blanket clearance
Section 42 consent is distinct from SMC
GIS geometry must retain version date
designation boundary does not prove exact buried archaeological extent
NHLE/GIS evidence does not replace site investigation
scheduled status does not determine development yield
consent conditions and validity periods must be retained
de-designated status must not be treated as current scheduling
public access cannot be inferred from scheduling
absence from one derivative dataset is not definitive absence from NHLE
no parcel heritage clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official Historic England, Planning Data, GOV.UK and legislation.gov.uk sources checked on 2026-07-26. July 2026 collection/GIS/SMC currentity was preserved with SMC/planning/Section42/Class Consent/title separation; no parcel promotion.
